registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: Multiple myeloma is a plasma cell neoplasm that can cause painful bone lesions. The main treatment for these lesions and pain control is radiotherapy, usually in daily fractions. In 2017, a phase III study proved the effectiveness of using a single dose of 8 Gy, but without description of several important oncological outcomes. This is a single-arm prospective cohort study. This study aims to describe these outcomes, including retreatment rate and bone events. Also, as secondary objectives, describe the quality of life and use of analgesic medications in this population.

registry_schema.text: Radiotherapy alone is the standard treatment for early stage NPC. In retrospective study of early stage NPC patients treated with radiotherapy alone. In the present trial, we hope to assess the value of concurrent chemotherapy and radiotherapy in patients with stage II (T1-2N1) NPC.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective multicenter single-arm phase 2 trial for newly diagnosed EBV-positive nasopharyngeal carcinoma in children and adults. Patients are allocated, not randomized, by age, induction response, and metastases. Induction for non-metastatic disease is three cycles of cisplatin 100 mg/m2 over 6 hours and 5-fluorouracil 1000 mg/m2/day for 5 days, with nivolumab 4.5 mg/kg (maximum 360 mg) every 3 weeks.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Radiotherapy and concurrent chemotherapy then follow one of five protocol pathways.

arms.label: Age 25 or younger, non-metastatic, complete or partial response
arms.text: Nivolumab stops after three induction doses. Partial response: 45.0 Gy to the elective volume and a boost to 59.4 Gy at 1.8 Gy per fraction. Complete response: boost reduced so total dose is 54.0 Gy. Concurrent cisplatin 20 mg/m2 on days 1-3 of the first and last radiotherapy week, then interferon-beta maintenance.

arms.label: Age 25 or younger, stable or progressive disease, or initial metastases
arms.text: Nivolumab continues through chemoradiotherapy for six doses, or seven if metastatic disease responds and a fourth chemotherapy cycle is given. Chemoradiotherapy uses the same dose rules as the responding non-metastatic group.

arms.label: Age older than 25, non-metastatic, complete or partial response
arms.text: Same three-cycle induction. Radiotherapy 66-70.2 Gy by adult guidelines. Concurrent cisplatin totaling 200-300 mg/m2 by local practice. No interferon maintenance.

arms.label: Age older than 25, stable or progressive disease, or initial metastases
arms.text: Non-response uses the adult chemoradiotherapy doses with nivolumab continued for six doses. Initial metastases use three cycles of gemcitabine and cisplatin, nivolumab through chemoradiotherapy, and irradiation of metastases according to published guidelines. A fourth cycle and a seventh nivolumab dose are allowed after response.

registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: This is a randomized, phase III, prospective, multi-center trial in newly diagnosed nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) patients without distant metastasis. This study will evaluate whether omitting Level Va irradiation in patients without these risk features does not compromise regional control or survival, with the goal of providing robust evidence to guide further personalization of NPC radiotherapy.

registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: Locally recurrent nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) may be salvaged by intensity modulated-radiotherapy (IMRT), but severe late toxicities become the most common reason of death in IMRT salvaged NPC patients. The aim of this phase II randomized controlled study is to address the efficacy of concurrent Endostar (Endostatins) with IMRT to reduce the occurrence of severe late toxicities compared with IMRT alone for locally recurrent NPC patients.

schema.label: Step 1
schema.text: Register after financial clearance for proton therapy.

schema.label: Step 2
schema.text: Step 2 must occur no later than 30 days after Step 1. Stratify by histology (breast versus NSCLC), systemic disease status (active versus stable or none), and use of intrathecal therapy and/or immunotherapy and/or targeted therapy, including antibody-drug conjugates, within 4 weeks before Step 2 and/or planned within 4 weeks after RT (yes versus no). Randomize 1:1. Protocol treatment starts within 21 days after randomization. Intrathecal therapy is not given on radiotherapy days in either arm. Systemic therapy may be given on radiation days at investigator discretion. Primary endpoint is overall survival.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Involved-field photon RT, 3 Gy x 10 daily fractions, to focal radiographic and/or symptomatic sites, then standard-of-care therapy per the investigator. Treatment of the entire craniospinal compartment is not allowed.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Proton craniospinal irradiation, 3 Gy x 10 daily fractions, to the entire craniospinal compartment, then standard-of-care therapy per the investigator. Proton dose is reported in Gy (RBE) with RBE 1.1.

eligibility: Step 1: Pathologically, histologically or cytologically, proven breast cancer or NSCLC, age 18 or older, and a candidate for radiation for leptomeningeal metastasis. The patient must be able to undergo MRI with and without gadolinium.

Newly diagnosed leptomeningeal metastasis, shown by positive CSF cytology, or by radiographic linear and/or nodular disease plus typical clinical signs meeting EANO-ESMO diagnostic criteria type IIA to IIC when cytology is equivocal or negative or CSF sampling is not suitable. CSF cytology with suspicious cells is positive. Atypical cells are equivocal and are not positive. For prior or current immunotherapy, CSF sampling rather than MRI enhancement alone is strongly recommended, to exclude immune-related aseptic meningitis.

Step 2 registration is no later than 30 days after Step 1 and requires financial clearance for proton therapy, standard-of-care systemic imaging such as CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis or body PET/CT, and Karnofsky performance status at least 60.
Not pregnant and not nursing. A person of childbearing potential needs a negative urine or serum pregnancy test within 14 days before registration.

Hemoglobin at least 8.0 g/dL, ANC at least 1,000/mm3, and platelets at least 100,000/mm3. Transfusion, growth factor, or another intervention may be used to meet those blood counts. Total bilirubin at or under 1.5 x institutional ULN. Gilbert disease without other clinically significant liver abnormalities is not excluded. AST and ALT at or under 3 x ULN.

No prior radiation to the spinal cord with EQD2 more than 40 Gy, or to the cauda equina with EQD2 more than 50 Gy, using an alpha/beta ratio of 3. No prior treatment for leptomeningeal metastasis. Prior CNS treatment for other non-leptomeningeal disease is allowed.

No history of unstable angina requiring hospitalization in the last 3 months. No myocardial infarction within the last 3 months. NYHA class III or IV is not eligible, and class II or better is required. No active infection currently requiring intravenous antibiotics. No active COPD exacerbation or other acute respiratory illness precluding study therapy. No CTCAE v5.0 grade 2 or higher encephalopathy.

registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: The landmark trials that established breast conservation therapy (BCT) (breast-conserving surgery followed by adjuvant breast irradiation) as a suitable alternative to mastectomy were conducted in an era that predated biological subtyping of breast cancer and the use of HER2-directed therapies in patients with HER2+ cancers. These trials established adjuvant radiotherapy following breast-conserving surgery as necessary to maximize local control, yet, in the intervening years, overall outcomes have improved significantly owing to widespread adoption of screening mammography, resulting in a substantial reduction in average tumor size at diagnosis, as well as improvements in surgical technique…

schema.label: Population
schema.text: Premenopausal, resected ER-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer: pN0 with Oncotype RS 21-25, or RS 16-20 with high clinical risk (low grade and >3 cm, intermediate grade and >2 cm, or high grade and >1 cm); or pN1 with RS 0-25.

schema.label: Step 1: Pre-entry
schema.text: Registration. Patients qualifying by MammaPrint Low Risk/MP1 need central Oncotype DX RS before randomization; MammaPrint High Risk/MP2 are ineligible. Intended RT plan declared before pre-entry.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Nodal/RS status (pN0 RS 16-25 vs pN1 RS 0-15 vs pN1 RS 16-25), intent to receive a CDK4/6 inhibitor (yes vs no), age (18-39 vs 40 or older).

schema.label: Step 2: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Stratified permuted blocks.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Ovarian function suppression (GnRH agonist of investigator's choice, or bilateral oophorectomy) plus aromatase inhibitor for 5 years.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Adjuvant chemotherapy of investigator's choice (NCCN- or ESMO-listed regimen), then ovarian function suppression plus aromatase inhibitor for 5 years.

schema.label: Radiotherapy (both arms)
schema.text: Whole breast irradiation required after lumpectomy (partial breast irradiation not permitted); post-mastectomy and regional nodal RT per protocol guidelines by nodal status. Allowed WBI regimens: 50 Gy/25, 42.56 Gy/16, 40 Gy/15, or 26 Gy/5, with optional sequential or concomitant boost. OFS plus AI preferably started before and given with RT, or within 4 weeks after RT.

schema.label: Other therapy
schema.text: CDK4/6 inhibitor (abemaciclib or other FDA-approved) and bone anti-resorptive therapy allowed per standard use.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Invasive breast cancer-free survival.

eligibility: Female, age 18 or older; ECOG 0-2 (or Karnofsky 60% or more).

Premenopausal: age 50 or under with menses within 12 months; age >50-60 with menses within 12 months plus premenopausal FSH and estradiol; or premenopausal FSH and estradiol if amenorrheic from IUD, uterine ablation, or prior hysterectomy.
Resected pT1-3 (T1c or higher if N0), pN0 or pN1 (pN1mi, pN1a-c) by AJCC 8th edition. ITCs count as N0; micrometastases (0.2-2 mm) count as N1.

Oncotype DX RS: pN0 requires RS 21-25, or RS 16-20 with high clinical risk; pN1 (1-3 nodes) requires RS below 26. MammaPrint Low Risk/MP1 patients need central Oncotype testing; MammaPrint High Risk/MP2 ineligible.
ER and/or PgR positive (1% or more by IHC) and HER2-negative by ASCO/CAP, local testing.

Lumpectomy, or total, skin-sparing, or nipple-sparing mastectomy. Lumpectomy margins free of invasive cancer and DCIS (no ink on tumor; positive posterior margin allowed if no further resection possible; LCIS at margin allowed). Mastectomy margins free of gross tumor; microscopic positive margin allowed if chest wall PMRT is planned.
Axillary staging by sentinel node biopsy, targeted axillary dissection, or ALND.
No more than 16 weeks from last breast surgery (including re-excision) to pre-entry.
Synchronous ipsilateral or contralateral, multifocal, or multicentric cancer allowed if the highest-stage tumor qualifies and other sites would not need chemotherapy or HER2-directed therapy.

No prior RT, chemotherapy, or biotherapy for the current breast cancer. Endocrine therapy for this cancer limited to less than 6 weeks (neoadjuvant or adjuvant). Prior preventive tamoxifen and AI or GnRH for fertility preservation allowed.
No metastatic disease, pT4 or inflammatory breast cancer, or non-epithelial breast malignancy (sarcoma, lymphoma).
No prior invasive breast cancer in either breast (prior DCIS or LCIS allowed; prior ipsilateral DCIS treated with lumpectomy and RT requires mastectomy for the current cancer).
No life expectancy under 10 years from comorbidity.

No ANC below 1,200/mm3, platelets below 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin below 10 g/dL, bilirubin above ULN (above 1.5 x ULN with Gilbert's), AST/ALT above 3 x ULN, or GFR below 30 mL/min/1.73m2 on most recent routine labs.
Patients with cardiac history, cardiac symptoms, or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class 2B or better.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months. Chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy; HCV must be treated and cured or have undetectable viral load on therapy.
Prior or concurrent non-breast malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Hormonal contraception (including progestin IUDs) must be stopped before pre-entry. Not pregnant and not nursing.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Colorectal cancer incidence in years 4 through 11 (non-inferiority of the 10-year-only schedule).

eligibility: Age 45 or older and under 70 at the time of the qualifying colonoscopy.

First-time diagnosis of 1-2 non-advanced tubular adenomas (under 10 mm, no tubulovillous or villous features, no high-grade or severe dysplasia) on a qualifying colonoscopy within 4 years before randomization. Sessile serrated polyps that do not meet advanced criteria count as non-advanced.
Qualifying colonoscopy complete to the cecum with adequate preparation, with complete excision of all adenomatous polyps (excision of hyperplastic rectosigmoid polyps not required).
Able to read or understand English or Spanish.
No prior colorectal cancer or colorectal adenoma (including sessile serrated lesions) other than those found on the qualifying colonoscopy.
No hyperplastic polyp 1 cm or larger, either previously or on the qualifying colonoscopy. No traditional serrated adenoma on the qualifying colonoscopy.
No colonoscopy between the qualifying colonoscopy and randomization.
No subtotal colectomy or total proctocolectomy (segmental resection allowed).
No first-degree relative with CRC diagnosed at age 60 or younger, and no two first-degree relatives with CRC at any age.
No clinical diagnosis or known germline mutation for familial adenomatous polyposis or Lynch syndrome. No inflammatory bowel disease.
No prior malignancy unless disease-free for 5 or more years and at low risk of recurrence; in situ cancers and basal or squamous cell skin cancer within 5 years allowed.
No life expectancy under 10 years from comorbidity, and no condition that would prevent colonoscopy or follow-up.

schema.text: Age 35-50 with a germline pathogenic or likely pathogenic BRCA1 mutation, at least one ovary and fallopian tube in situ. Non-randomized: surgery chosen by the patient after standardized counseling that RRSO is standard of care.

schema.label: BLS cohort
schema.text: Bilateral salpingectomy with delayed oophorectomy (concurrent hysterectomy allowed), within 180 days of registration. Annual re-counseling that oophorectomy by age 40 is recommended; crossover to completion oophorectomy allowed any time, analyzed intention-to-treat.

schema.label: BSO cohort
schema.text: Risk-reducing bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (concurrent hysterectomy allowed), within 180 days of registration. HRT encouraged after BSO if no contraindication.

schema.label: Pathology
schema.text: SEE-FIM processing of all specimens; STIC or invasive cancer sent for central review.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Time to incident high-grade serous ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian tube carcinoma (non-inferiority of BLS to BSO).

eligibility: Age 35-50, inclusive; premenopausal or menopausal.
Pathogenic or likely pathogenic germline BRCA1 mutation on CLIA-approved testing, documented.
Planned RRSO (BSO cohort), or declined or deferred BSO after counseling and undergoing salpingectomy (BLS cohort). Concurrent hysterectomy allowed.

At least one intact ovary and fallopian tube at counseling, consent, and registration. Prior hysterectomy allowed if it did not include bilateral salpingectomy; prior tubal ligation allowed if one ovary and tube with fimbria remain.
Pelvic ultrasound (transvaginal preferred) or pelvic MRI and CA-125 within 180 days before registration.
Current pregnancy or planned future pregnancy by assisted reproduction allowed after counseling; salpingectomy at planned cesarean section allowed.

No cytotoxic chemotherapy for a prior cancer within the past 30 days. No prior radiotherapy to the abdomen or pelvis at any time. Endocrine therapy and maintenance HER2-targeted, immune checkpoint inhibitor, or PARP inhibitor therapy allowed.
No prior ovarian cancer (including low malignant potential tumors), primary peritoneal carcinoma, or fallopian tube carcinoma.

No screening abnormality suspicious for pelvic malignancy within 180 days: imaging with morphology suspicious for ovarian cancer (simple cysts and benign-appearing complex cysts allowed), or CA-125 above 50 U/mL (premenopausal, no oral contraceptives), above 40 U/mL (premenopausal on oral contraceptives), or above 35 U/mL (postmenopausal).
Medically fit for the planned surgery.

Able to understand, speak, read, and write English or Spanish; willing to take part in a 6-week mindfulness program; able to use a smartphone, tablet, or other digital device.
No history or current evidence of recurrent or metastatic breast cancer.
No current or prior other cancer, except non-melanoma skin cancer or in situ cervical cancer not treated with chemotherapy.
Not pregnant or planning pregnancy in the near future.
Not enrolled in another cancer control or behavioral intervention trial requiring frequent assessments or training.

schema.label: Step 1
schema.text: Register for central pathology review confirming glioblastoma histology and unmethylated MGMT promoter status, and for central review that baseline neurocognitive scores are in range. Tumor tissue must be received and central review completed, and all neurocognitive tests completed, before Step 2.

schema.label: Step 2
schema.text: Stratify by RPA class (III versus IV versus V), radiation fractionation intent (conventional 6000 cGy in 30 fractions versus hypofractionated 4000 cGy in 15 fractions), and intent to use tumor treating fields (yes versus no). Randomize 1:1. No more than 50% of randomized patients may be younger than 65. Age is part of RPA class and is not its own stratification factor. RPA III is age under 50 and KPS 90-100. RPA IV is age under 50 with KPS under 90, or age 50 or older with KPS 70-100 and no worse than minor neurologic impairment. RPA V is age 50 or older with KPS 70-100 and worse than minor neurologic impairment. Protocol treatment starts within 8 weeks after surgery. Primary endpoint is time to neurocognitive failure.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Standard photon RT, 6000 cGy at 200 cGy per day for 30 fractions or 4000 cGy at 267 cGy per day for 15 fractions, with temozolomide 75 mg/m2 daily during RT, then adjuvant temozolomide 150-200 mg/m2 on days 1-5 of each 28-day cycle for 6 cycles. Tumor treating fields may start in the adjuvant phase after the post-concurrent brain MRI.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Temporally modulated pulsed RT at the same total dose and daily dose as Arm 1. Each daily treatment is 10-13 pulses of 20 cGy with a 3-minute interval between pulses. Concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide, and tumor treating fields, are the same as Arm 1.

eligibility: Step 1: Age 18 or older, Karnofsky performance status at least 70, and proficient in English or French Canadian, with no known IDH mutation, and a patient already known to have an IDH mutation on local or other testing is ineligible and should not be registered.

Surgical resection is required, stereotactic biopsy alone is not allowed, and an FFPE tumor block and H&E slide must be shipped to the NYU Center for Biospecimen Research and Development on or before postoperative calendar day 30 for central histology and MGMT promoter review.

If that tissue cannot ship by postoperative day 30, the patient may not enroll, because treatment must start no later than 8 weeks after surgery, and after a further resection the tissue must ship within 30 days of the most recent resection, which itself must be within 30 days of the initial resection.

Not pregnant and not nursing, with a negative urine or serum pregnancy test within 14 days before Step 1 for a person of childbearing potential, and no known leptomeningeal disease or metastatic disease outside the brain.

Hemoglobin at least 10 g/dL, with transfusion or another intervention allowed, leukocytes at least 2,000/mm3 or ANC at least 1,500/mm3, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, creatinine clearance at least 50 mL/min, total bilirubin at or under 1.5 x institutional ULN, and AST and ALT at or under 3 x ULN.
No prior cranial radiation that would overlap treatment fields, and no previous therapy for glioblastoma except surgery, laser interstitial thermal therapy, or a Gliadel wafer.
ALA-mediated fluorescence-guided resection, photodynamic therapy, or fluorescein given to aid resection is allowed and is not counted as chemotherapy or an intracerebral agent.
No unstable angina requiring hospitalization in the last 3 months, no myocardial infarction within the last 3 months, and NYHA class III or IV is not eligible (class II or better is required).

No active infection currently requiring intravenous antibiotics, no COPD exacerbation or other acute respiratory illness precluding study therapy, no movement disorder that would prevent lying still in an immobilization mask for about 40 minutes, no significant sensory deficit such as blindness or mutism that would prohibit neurocognitive testing, and no history of allergic reaction to temozolomide or a related compound such as dacarbazine.

HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible, chronic hepatitis B requires an undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated, hepatitis C must have been treated and cured or current treatment must have an undetectable viral load, and a prior or concurrent malignancy is allowed when it will not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

Step 2: Central review must confirm IDH-wildtype glioblastoma with an unmethylated MGMT promoter, standard-of-care IDH testing by at least one method such as immunohistochemistry for IDH1 R132H must show no mutation, and insufficient or inadequate tissue, failed MGMT testing, or an indeterminate or methylated MGMT promoter is excluded.

Baseline HVLT-R, Trail Making Test, and COWA within 28 days before Step 2 must meet HVLT-R Total Recall greater than 5, Delayed Recall greater than 3, Delayed Recognition greater than -10, Trail Making Test Part A at or under 2738, Part B at or under 3724, and COWA at least 12, and scores outside those ranges are excluded.

eligibility: Age 18 or older; ECOG 0-1.
Histologically confirmed stage IIB, IIC, or III colon adenocarcinoma (AJCC 8th edition) with en bloc R0 resection (two-stage procedures after decompressive colostomy allowed).
Tumor distal extent 12 cm or more from the anal verge or above the peritoneal reflection (no rectal cancer warranting chemoradiation).
MSS or intact MMR proteins by CLIA-approved or accredited testing; MSI-H/dMMR excluded.
Adequate tumor tissue and postoperative blood for central Signatera ctDNA testing (no transfusion within 2 weeks before the ctDNA draw).
Study entry between postoperative day 7 and day 60.

No radiographic metastatic disease on CT or MRI of chest, abdomen, and pelvis within 45 days before entry; no pathologic or clinical metastases, including resected non-contiguous intra-abdominal metastases.
Candidate for all study agents (5-FU, leucovorin, oxaliplatin, irinotecan) and able to tolerate 6 months of combination chemotherapy.

ANC 1,500/mm3 or more (1,300 or more with benign ethnic neutropenia), platelets 100,000/mm3 or more, hemoglobin 9 g/dL or more; bilirubin at or below ULN, alkaline phosphatase and AST/ALT below 2.5 x ULN; creatinine 1.5 x ULN or less or CrCl 50 mL/min or more, all within 28 days.
No histology other than adenocarcinoma, tumor-related bowel perforation, synchronous colon or rectal primary, or prior invasive colon cancer.
No prior chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, or radiation for colorectal cancer (cancers warranting neoadjuvant therapy excluded), apart from the single optional cycle.
No other invasive malignancy within 5 years (colonic polyps, non-melanoma skin cancer, and carcinoma in situ allowed).
No bone marrow or solid organ transplant. HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
No grade 2 or higher neuropathy, known homozygous DPD deficiency, Gilbert's syndrome, or homozygous UGT1A1*28.
Patients with cardiac history, cardiac symptoms, or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class 2B or better. No uncontrolled seizure disorder or active infection requiring systemic therapy.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

Second randomization (Cohort A Arm 2 converters): ctDNA positive on monitoring, reaffirmed consent, ECOG 0-1, no metastatic disease on imaging, same lab thresholds within 28 days, still a candidate for FOLFOX, CAPOX, and mFOLFIRINOX.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Standard of care: continue chemotherapy, or standard-dose chemoradiation of 50.4 Gy or 54.0 Gy in 1.8 Gy fractions, or observation. Observation is suggested only for patients who completed 6 months of chemotherapy before enrollment.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Dose-escalated RT. The default prescription is 10 Gy x 5 fractions (BED10 100 Gy). If 5 fractions are not feasible, 3 Gy x 25 fractions (BED10 97.5 Gy) may be used after contact with the principal investigator or a radiation oncology chair.

eligibility: Pathologically proven pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma that is locally advanced and unresectable by NCCN guidelines and institutional tumor board review. Age 18 or older and ECOG performance status 0-2. Baseline pre-chemotherapy staging must be CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, CT chest with MRI abdomen and pelvis, CT chest and pelvis with MRI abdomen, or PET/CT.

Before enrollment the patient must have received 4-8 months of active chemotherapy with mFOLFIRINOX, FOLFIRINOX, or NALIRIFOX, or with gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel. Active time excludes treatment breaks. More than one regimen is allowed for toxicity or for CA19-9 that is not declining, not for radiographic progression by RECIST. Chemotherapy after restaging is allowed if restaging is after at least 4 months and total chemotherapy duration does not exceed 8 months. Registration must be within 45 days of the last day of that chemotherapy.
A prior or concurrent malignancy is eligible when its natural history or treatment will not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment of the neoadjuvant regimen or the primary endpoint.

Labs any time before chemotherapy through 30 days after chemotherapy starts: ALT and AST at or under 3 x ULN. If baseline CA19-9 is above 37 U/mL, the concurrent bilirubin must be at or under 1.5 x ULN, and both may be repeated until bilirubin is at or under 1.5 x ULN within that window. If baseline CA19-9 is at or under 37 U/mL, concurrent bilirubin is unrestricted.

After month 4 of chemotherapy and before study entry, if baseline CA19-9 was above 37 U/mL, the later CA19-9 must be under 200 U/mL or at least a 70% decline from baseline. A value of 200 U/mL or higher still qualifies if the decline is at least 70%, and a decline under 70% still qualifies if the absolute value is under 200 U/mL. If baseline CA19-9 was at or under 37 U/mL, it must remain at or under 37 U/mL.
Restaging CT, MRI, or PET/CT must show at least stable disease. No active duodenal or gastric ulcers. No direct tumor invasion of the bowel or stomach.
No prior radiotherapy to the region of the study cancer that would overlap radiation fields. Prior non-overlapping radiation, for example breast, head and neck, or extremity, is permitted.

Not pregnant and not nursing. No cardiac condition that was the primary reason for hospitalization in the last 6 months. NYHA class III or IV is not eligible, and class II or better is required. HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible.

eligibility: HCC with macrovascular invasion: enhancing thrombus with arterial enhancement and washout. Extrahepatic disease is allowed.
At most 5 discrete intrahepatic foci. Sum of diameters under 20 cm. No direct extension into stomach, duodenum, small bowel, or large bowel.
No fibrolamellar, sarcomatoid, or biphenotypic HCC. Child-Pugh A or B7. ECOG 0-2. Age 18 or older.
Pathologic confirmation is strongly recommended. A radiographic AASLD diagnosis is allowed, except when there is a prior or concurrent malignancy, in which case pathology is required.

arms.text: SABR to the primary tumor, 42 Gy in 3 fractions, plus standard immunotherapy.

eligibility: Pathologically proven renal cell carcinoma. Node-positive unresectable (TxN1Mx) or metastatic (TxNxM1), with history and physical and CT or MRI of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis within 45 days. IMDC intermediate or poor risk. A prior or concurrent malignancy is allowed when it will not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 outside the primary renal tumor. Not recommended for immediate cytoreductive nephrectomy, or refused it. A candidate for standard IO-IO or IO-VEGF therapy. Primary tumor 20 cm or less in anterior-to-posterior dimension on axial imaging.

Age 18 or older and Karnofsky performance status greater than 60 within 45 days. Within 45 days: hemoglobin greater than 8 g/dL (transfusion allowed), platelets greater than 50,000/mm3, ANC greater than 1,500/mm3, and creatinine clearance greater than 30 mL/min. For the stated African American calculation exception, CKD-EPI GFR at least 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 is adequate.
Hepatic function within 45 days: total bilirubin under 1.5 x ULN (under 3.0 mg/dL with Gilbert syndrome), and AST and ALT under 3 x ULN, or under 5 x ULN with liver metastases.

Known HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible. Testing is not required. Chronic hepatitis B requires an undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated. Hepatitis C must be treated and cured, or current treatment must have an undetectable viral load.

Agree to highly effective contraception, including men with vasectomies who have sex with a woman of childbearing potential. Informed consent, and US authorization to release health information, before entry.

Ineligible if all metastatic disease is planned for definitive surgery, ablative radiation, or other intervention that would leave no extra-renal measurable disease. Palliative radiation sites are not used for response. Untreated or unstable brain metastases or cranial epidural disease are excluded. Treated brain metastases are eligible when no steroids are required and there is no progression or hemorrhage for at least 4 weeks, documented by MRI or CT or judged stable by the investigator.

No prior radiotherapy to the kidney that would overlap treatment of the primary. No systemic therapy for metastatic renal cell carcinoma started more than 90 days before registration. Prior chemotherapy for a different cancer is allowed if completed more than 3 years before registration.

No severe active comorbidity as listed in section 3.2.5, including autoimmune disease on daily corticosteroids above 10 mg prednisone equivalent or other daily immunosuppression, severe hypersensitivity to chimeric or humanized antibodies, active tuberculosis, uncontrolled hypertension above 190 systolic or 110 diastolic, major surgery with hospital admission within 28 days, a serious non-healing wound, ulcer, or fracture within 45 days, an arterial thrombotic event within 180 days, NYHA class 3-4 symptoms, Child-Pugh B or C, untreated pulmonary embolism or DVT within 180 days, unstable arrhythmia within 180 days, or fistula, perforation, abscess, obstruction, inflammatory bowel disease, or malabsorption in the windows in section 3.2.5. Treated asymptomatic pulmonary embolism, or treated asymptomatic DVT more than 30 days earlier, is allowed. Inhaled steroids and adrenal replacement above 10 mg prednisone equivalent are allowed when autoimmune disease is not active.
Pregnancy, and people unwilling to stop nursing, are excluded. A woman of childbearing potential needs a negative pregnancy test within 45 days before registration.

Age 18 or older. ECOG 0-2. Not pregnant and not nursing. A pregnancy test within 14 days is required for persons of childbearing potential.
Adequate hematologic, renal, and hepatic function, per the required initial laboratory values in section 3.2.6.

Age 18 or older. Zubrod performance status 0-2.

arms.text: Patients undergo pelvic EBRT daily for 5-6 weeks and vaginal brachytherapy completed within 7 days after completion of EBRT in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Patients also undergo collection of blood samples and CT scans, MRI scans, or x-ray imaging throughout the trial.

eligibility: Recurrent endometrial cancer with measurable disease (RECIST 1.1) or non-measurable detectable disease (small lesions, tumor-related ascites or effusion, or non-target imaging abnormalities).
Mismatch repair deficient by institutional IHC (loss of MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6, or EPCAM) and/or MSI-high by MSI testing or NGS; equivocal IHC allowed with documented MSI.
Histology: endometrioid, mucinous, dedifferentiated/undifferentiated, clear cell, mixed epithelial, or adenocarcinoma NOS. No serous carcinoma or carcinosarcoma.

1-2 prior lines of systemic therapy. Prior anti-PD-1/PD-L1 allowed only if given with chemotherapy or RT in the adjuvant or primary metastatic/recurrent setting, with CR and a treatment-free interval of 12 months or more since the last checkpoint inhibitor dose.

Prior RT for endometrial cancer (pelvic, extended field, vaginal brachytherapy, palliative) allowed if completed at least 4 weeks before registration. Hormonal therapy stopped at least 3 weeks before; other anticancer therapy at least 4 weeks before (6 weeks for nitrosoureas or mitomycin C). At least 4 weeks since major surgery.
Age 18 or older; ECOG 0-2.

Platelets 100,000/mcL or more, ANC 1,500/mcL or more, creatinine 1.5 x ULN or less, bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less (3 x ULN or less with Gilbert's), AST and ALT 3 x ULN or less, within 14 days. Oxygen saturation with hypoxia below grade 2 within 28 days.
Patients with cardiac history, cardiac symptoms, or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class 2B or better with QTc below 450 msec.
Treated brain metastases allowed if follow-up imaging shows no progression and the patient is stable off steroids for at least 1 month.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated; HCV must be treated and cured or undetectable on treatment.

No prior CTLA-4 inhibitor or other T-cell co-stimulation or checkpoint agent beyond the allowed anti-PD-1/PD-L1. No grade 3-4 or recurrent grade 2 immune-related toxicity on prior anti-PD-1/PD-L1 that led to delay or discontinuation.

No active autoimmune disease or history of autoimmune disease that might recur and affect vital organs or need systemic immunosuppression (vitiligo, replaced endocrinopathies, and topically controlled psoriasis allowed). No known immune impairment.
No chronic steroids above prednisone 10 mg daily or equivalent, and no immunosuppressive therapy (inhaled, topical, intranasal, local injections, and hypersensitivity premedication allowed).
No uncontrolled intercurrent illness, including active infection, interstitial lung disease or non-infectious pneumonitis, symptomatic heart failure, unstable angina, or arrhythmia.
No severe hypersensitivity to monoclonal antibodies or to nivolumab or ipilimumab.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

schema.label: US assignment
schema.text: This file is the NRG appendix to CCTG EN.10, not a randomized schema. US patients enroll to EN.10A, RAINBO BLUE, POLE-mutated, Cohort A1 only, or to EN.10B, TAPER, p53 wild type or NSMP. US sites do not participate in Cohort A2. Table 1 then assigns adjuvant management by stage and molecular group. This file plans 120 POLE-mutated Cohort A1 patients and 180 p53wt/NSMP patients, recruited in 3 years. Molecular results should allow protocol treatment or active surveillance within 10 weeks of hysterectomy and staging.

schema.label: Cohort A1, POLE-mutated
schema.text: Histotype may be endometrioid, serous, clear cell, undifferentiated or dedifferentiated, carcinosarcoma, or mixed. LVI is none, focal if fewer than 3 foci, or substantial or extensive if 3 or more foci.

arms.label: Group A1.1

arms.label: Group A1.2
arms.text: Observation. Stage IA not confined to a polyp, grade 3, pN0, with no LVI or focal LVI; or stage IB, grade 3, pN0, with no LVI or focal LVI; or microscopic stage II, grade 1 or 2, pN0, with no LVI or focal LVI.

arms.label: Group A1.3
arms.text: Observation. Stage IA not confined to a polyp, grade 3, pN0, with substantial or extensive LVI; or stage IB, grade 1 or 2, pNx or pN0, with substantial or extensive LVI.

schema.label: Sub-study B, p53wt/NSMP
schema.text: Endometrioid histology only, and ER positive. p53wt/NSMP carcinoma with MELF myoinvasion and/or substantial or extensive LVI is not eligible.

arms.label: Group B1
arms.text: Observation. Same stage group as A1.1: stage IB, grade 1 or 2, pNx or pN0, with no LVI or focal LVI.

arms.label: Group B2
arms.text: Vaginal brachytherapy. Same stage group as A1.2.

schema.label: Radiation doses, when radiation is given
schema.text: Table 1 assigns observation or vaginal brachytherapy to the groups above and does not assign pelvic EBRT to them. Section 10.1 still prints the NRG template. EBRT, when used, is IMRT to the upper vagina and pelvic nodes: 45 Gy in 25 daily fractions of 1.8 Gy, or 48.6 Gy in 27 daily fractions of 1.8 Gy. Brachytherapy alone: HDR 7.0 Gy x 3 prescribed at 0.5 cm depth (21 Gy), HDR 6.0 Gy x 5 to the surface (30 Gy), HDR 4.0 Gy x 6 to the surface (24 Gy), or PDR/LDR 60 Gy in 1 fraction to the surface. HDR boost after EBRT is 5.0 Gy x 2 to the surface, total EQD2 56.8 Gy after 45 Gy or 60.3 Gy after 48.6 Gy. PDR/LDR boost is 25 Gy in 1 fraction to the surface, total surface dose 70 Gy after 45 Gy or 73.6 Gy after 48.6 Gy. Per protocol, EBRT starts 6-8 weeks after surgery, with 4-12 weeks acceptable. The appendix says full sub-study details are in the master protocol.

eligibility: Complete molecular classification is required before inclusion, on the hysterectomy specimen or the preoperative specimen: POLE exonuclease-domain mutation status, MMR immunohistochemistry, ER immunohistochemistry, and p53 immunohistochemistry or TP53 sequencing, reported by an accredited laboratory. NGS is acceptable when those data are available in time for protocol treatment within 10 weeks of surgical staging.
US sites enroll only EN.10A Cohort A1, RAINBO BLUE, for POLE-mutated cancer, or EN.10B, TAPER, for p53 wild type or NSMP cancer. US sites will not participate in Cohort A2.
POLE-mutated histotypes may be endometrioid, serous, clear cell, undifferentiated or dedifferentiated, carcinosarcoma, or mixed. p53wt/NSMP disease must be endometrioid and ER positive.

Eligible stage groups are those in Table 1: stage IB, grade 1 or 2, pNx or pN0, with no or focal LVI; stage IA not confined to a polyp, grade 3, pN0, with no or focal LVI; stage IB, grade 3, pN0, with no or focal LVI; microscopic stage II, grade 1 or 2, pN0, with no or focal LVI; and, for POLE-mutated Cohort A1 only, stage IA grade 3 pN0 or stage IB grade 1 or 2 pNx or pN0 with substantial or extensive LVI.

p53wt/NSMP endometrial carcinoma with a MELF pattern of myoinvasion and/or substantial or extensive lymphovascular invasion is not eligible. Focal LVI is fewer than 3 foci. Substantial or extensive LVI is 3 or more foci.
HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible.

Histology: endometrioid, serous, dedifferentiated/undifferentiated, clear cell, mixed epithelial, carcinosarcoma, or adenocarcinoma NOS.

No active autoimmune disease or history of autoimmune disease that might recur and need immunosuppression (vitiligo, type 1 diabetes, replaced thyroiditis allowed). No steroid-requiring or current non-infectious pneumonitis. No stem cell or solid organ transplant.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated; HCV must be treated and cured or undetectable on treatment.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
No allergy to study agents or similar compounds. No interval or cytoreductive surgery on study before progression.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

eligibility: Newly diagnosed FIGO stage III or IV ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer: high-grade serous, high-grade endometrioid, carcinosarcoma, or other epithelial histology with a BRCA1/2 alteration. Known MMR-deficient/MSI-high or POLE-ultramutated tumors excluded (non-serous types).

Documented pathogenic or suspected pathogenic BRCA1/2 variant (tumor or germline), or BRCA wild-type with HRD-positive tumor by a CLIA-certified laboratory (for example Myriad MyChoice); report required.
Primary or interval cytoreductive surgery.

Completed first-line platinum-based chemotherapy of 4-9 cycles (6 or more strongly recommended; reason documented if fewer). IV, IP, or neoadjuvant platinum allowed. No investigational agent during first-line chemotherapy.
PR or CR with no clinical evidence of progression after chemotherapy; randomized at least 3 and no more than 12 weeks after the last platinum dose.
No prior PARP inhibitor (olaparib, niraparib, rucaparib).
Treated brain metastases allowed if follow-up imaging shows no progression and the patient is neurologically stable off steroids.
Age 18 or older; ECOG 0-2.

ANC 1,500/mm3 or more, platelets 100,000/mm3 or more, hemoglobin 9 g/dL or more; CrCl above 30 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault); bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less (3 x ULN or less with Gilbert's); AST and ALT 3 x ULN or less.
Patients with cardiac history, cardiac symptoms, or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class 2B or better.
No history of MDS or AML, and no prior allogeneic bone marrow transplant.

No active infection requiring parenteral antibiotics; no intra-abdominal abscess, undiverted fistula, GI perforation or obstruction, or need for nasogastric or gastrostomy drainage; able to swallow oral medication.
No concomitant strong or moderate CYP3A inducers. No hypersensitivity to olaparib or its excipients.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated; HCV must be treated and cured or undetectable on treatment.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

schema.label: Population
schema.text: Newly diagnosed squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, or adenosquamous carcinoma of the cervix, FIGO 2018 stage IIIA, IIIB, IIIC1, IIIC2, or IVA.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: FIGO stage III versus IVA, and presence or absence of para-aortic nodes (N2). Randomize 1:1.

schema.label: Arm 1
schema.text: Concurrent chemoradiation: weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 for 5 weeks, external-beam radiotherapy, brachytherapy, and pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for 5 cycles, then pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks for 14 maintenance cycles.

schema.label: Arm 2
schema.text: Induction weekly carboplatin AUC 2 and paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 for 6 weeks, plus pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for 2 cycles, then the same chemoradiation and pembrolizumab, then pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks for 15 maintenance cycles.

eligibility: Pathologically confirmed newly diagnosed cervical squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, or adenosquamous carcinoma.
Locally advanced disease: FIGO 2018 IIIA (T3aN0), IIIB (T3bN0), IIIC1 (T3aN1 or T3bN1), IIIC2 (T3aN2 or T3bN2), or IVA (T4aN0-N2).

No prior hysterectomy, defined as removal of the entire uterus. A prior partial hysterectomy for a reason other than cervical cancer may be allowed. No plan for hysterectomy as part of initial therapy.
No para-aortic node metastasis above the T12/L1 interspace. Node status may be confirmed by imaging or biopsy, as the protocol specifies.
No prior definitive surgery, radiation, or systemic therapy for cervical cancer. No prior immunotherapy. No prior pelvic radiotherapy for any disease.
ECOG performance status 2 or better. Not pregnant and not nursing.

ANC at least 1,500/mm3, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin at least 8 g/dL, creatinine clearance at least 50 mL/min, total bilirubin at most 1.5 times the upper limit, AST and ALT at most 3 times the upper limit.
No active infection requiring parenteral antibiotics. No live vaccine within 30 days. No immunodeficiency and no chronic systemic steroid therapy, as defined in the protocol.

No active autoimmune disease that required systemic treatment in the past 2 years. No history of non-infectious pneumonitis that required steroids, and no current pneumonitis. No allergic reaction to the study agents or similar compounds.

arms.label: Arm 2 (experimental)
arms.text: Sacituzumab govitecan-hziy 10 mg/kg IV Days 1 and 8 + bevacizumab (or biosimilar) 15 mg/kg IV Day 1, every 21 days. Internal toxicity assessment on the first 12 patients (rolling six design), no planned accrual suspension.

schema.label: Duration
schema.text: At least 6 and up to 10 cycles unless limited by intolerable AEs. Maintenance bevacizumab may start after 6 cycles and starts in all patients after 10 cycles (or earlier if chemotherapy/SG stopped for toxicity before 6 cycles). G-CSF prophylaxis allowed in both arms for high febrile neutropenia risk.

schema.label: Maintenance (both arms)

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Progression-free survival (RECIST 1.1, local investigator assessment).

eligibility: Histologic high-grade serous or endometrioid epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer.
Platinum-sensitive disease: progression documented ≥ 6 months (182 days) after the last platinum dose.
Progression during first-line maintenance PARP inhibitor for advanced disease, with no intervening therapy between PARPi progression and registration; last PARPi dose ≥ 3 weeks before registration.
Germline or somatic BRCA1/2 mutation, or HRD test positive.
Measurable or non-measurable disease per RECIST 1.1.
Age ≥ 18; ECOG performance status ≤ 2.
ANC ≥ 1,500/mm3, platelets ≥ 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL (transfusion allowed).
CrCl ≥ 30 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault); urinalysis ≤ 1+ protein or urine protein < 1.0 g/24 hr.
Total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN (≤ 3 x ULN with Gilbert's); AST and ALT ≤ 3 x ULN.
Patients with cardiac disease history, current symptoms, or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class 2B or better.
No prior topoisomerase-I inhibitor of any kind.
No investigational agents within 4 weeks of registration, and no concurrent non-study anticancer therapy.
Treated brain metastases allowed only with follow-up imaging 4 weeks after CNS-directed therapy showing no progression and disease stable off steroids.
No active infection requiring parenteral antibiotics; no non-healing wound, ulcer, or fracture.
No intra-abdominal abscess, undiverted abdominal/pelvic fistula, GI perforation, GI obstruction, or need for drainage NG or gastrostomy tube.
No clinically significant bleeding within 28 days; no uncontrolled hypertension (≥ 160 systolic or ≥ 100 diastolic).

No unresolved prior-therapy toxicity > grade 1 (except grade ≤ 2 neuropathy, alopecia, controlled hypertension or thyroid disease, thromboembolism on anticoagulation, and lab AEs meeting the lab criteria); no major surgery within 3 weeks.
No strong UGT1A1 inhibitors or inducers; no allergy to study agents or their excipients.

HIV allowed if on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load; HCV must be treated and cured or undetectable on treatment. Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing. Secondary or cytoreductive surgery on study before progression is not permitted.

schema.label: Step 1: Registration
schema.text: Early-stage oral cavity SCC, cT1-2N0 (AJCC 8th ed.). FDG PET/CT with central read.

schema.label: Step 2: Registration
schema.text: PET/CT node negative patients proceed to randomization. PET/CT node positive patients go off study (neck pathology recorded in a registry).

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Clinical and radiographic T stage (T1 vs T2); Zubrod performance status (0 vs 1-2).

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Primary tumor resection (transoral, aiming for 5 mm margins) and neck surgery in the same operation, within 30 days after central PET/CT review.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Sentinel lymph node biopsy with planar and mandatory SPECT/CT lymphatic mapping. Positive SLN leads to completion neck dissection (at least levels I-III) within 6 weeks, ideally 4.

arms.label: Arm 2 (control)
arms.text: Elective neck dissection, at least levels I-III (bilateral for lesions within 1 cm of midline).

schema.label: Adjuvant therapy (both arms, by final pathology)
schema.text: Observation if no adverse features. Adjuvant IMRT alone for PNI, LVI, pT3/T4, close margins (< 5 mm), or pN1+ (sites may omit RT for pN1 as the only risk factor). Adjuvant chemoradiation with concurrent cisplatin (every 3 weeks or weekly) for positive margins or extranodal extension. RT covers both primary site and at-risk neck: 60 Gy in 30 fractions (PTV_6000), 56 Gy in 30 (PTV_5600), 66 Gy in 30 (PTV_6600) when used. IMRT and IGRT mandatory, protons not allowed; adjuvant treatment starts within 42 days after surgery.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Phase II: patient-reported neck and shoulder function (NDII) at 6 months after surgery. Phase III: non-inferiority of disease-free survival plus NDII at 6 months.

schema.label: Sample size
schema.text: Phase II 258; phase III 686 total including phase II patients.

eligibility: Step 1: Histologically or cytologically proven SCC of the oral cavity (oral tongue, floor of mouth, mucosal lip, buccal mucosa, upper or lower alveolar ridge, retromolar trigone, or hard palate).

Step 1: Stage T1-2N0M0 (AJCC 8th ed.) by H&P, head and neck imaging (PET/CT, contrast neck CT, gadolinium neck MRI, or lateral and central neck ultrasound), and chest imaging, all within 42 days before registration.
Step 1: Surgical assessment within 42 days; candidate for SLN biopsy with possible completion neck dissection or END, with transoral resection of the primary expected to achieve free margins.
Step 1: Age ≥ 18; Zubrod performance status 0-2 within 42 days.
Step 1: Able to read a validated translation of the NDII.
Step 2: FDG PET/CT node negative by central read (ACR-accredited scanner; a pre-Step 1 PET/CT may be submitted) and baseline NDII completed.
No definitive clinical or radiologic evidence of cervical nodal or distant metastases.
No SCC of the oropharynx, nasopharynx, hypopharynx, or larynx.
No prior non-head and neck invasive malignancy unless disease free ≥ 2 years (non-melanoma skin cancer and carcinoma in situ of breast or cervix excepted).
No prior systemic chemotherapy for the study cancer (prior chemotherapy for a different cancer allowed).
No prior radiotherapy to the region that would overlap radiation fields.
No incomplete resection of the oral cavity lesion with a positive margin (excisional biopsy permitted).

No prior lateral neck surgery or neck injury precluding dissection (prior thyroid or central neck surgery and biopsy allowed); borderline nodes ≥ 1 cm thought benign should be sampled by ultrasound-guided FNA.
No hematologic malignancy (for example CLL) or other active disease that causes lymphadenopathy (for example sarcoidosis, untreated mycobacterial infection).
No active systemic cytotoxic chemotherapy or immunosuppressive, anti-monocyte, or immunomodulatory therapy; no participation in another investigational therapeutic trial.
No severe active comorbidity precluding neck dissection. Not pregnant and not breastfeeding (pregnancy test within 42 days if of childbearing potential).

Toxicities from prior chemotherapy or palliative RT recovered to ≤ grade 1.

HER2-positive cohort: no prior systemic therapy for unresectable, recurrent, or metastatic disease (prior neoadjuvant, adjuvant, or concurrent-with-RT therapy including HER2-directed, and androgen-receptor therapy in any setting, are allowed). HER2-low cohort: no prior HER2-directed therapy for unresectable, recurrent, or metastatic disease.
No unstable angina requiring hospitalization or MI within 6 months; no NYHA class III/IV; no persistent grade 3-4 electrolyte abnormalities; no active infection requiring IV antimicrobials.
No interstitial lung disease, pulmonary fibrosis, organizing pneumonia, drug-induced or idiopathic pneumonitis, or active pneumonitis on chest CT.
No grade ≥ 3 bleeding within 28 days; HER2-positive cohort: no > grade 3 peripheral neuropathy.
No prior cumulative anthracycline above doxorubicin 500 mg/m2, epirubicin 900 mg/m2, or mitoxantrone 120 mg/m2 (or doxorubicin equivalent); no allergy to the cohort's study agents.
HER2-low cohort: no live attenuated vaccine within 30 days before first dose.

HIV allowed on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy; HCV must be treated and cured or undetectable on treatment. Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

eligibility: Histologically or cytologically proven NPC with locoregional recurrence not amenable to curative surgery or re-irradiation, and/or distant metastases (de novo metastatic allowed).
EBV associated: EBER-positive tumor, or a history of detectable plasma EBV DNA by PCR at any time since diagnosis.

Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 (previously irradiated lesions count only with documented progression after RT); contrast CT chest, and contrast CT or MRI of nasopharynx and neck if locoregional disease is known.

Treated brain or leptomeningeal metastases or cord compression allowed if clinically stable ≥ 2 months and off steroids (> 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent) > 4 weeks; skull base involvement allowed unless directly invading brain with symptoms or significant edema.
Age ≥ 18; ECOG 0-2.
ANC ≥ 1,500/mm3, platelets ≥ 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin ≥ 8.0 g/dL (transfusion allowed, not EPO dependent).
Total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN or direct bilirubin ≤ ULN (≤ 3 x ULN with Gilbert's); ALT ≤ 3 x ULN (≤ 5 x ULN with liver metastases); corrected calcium ≤ 1.5 x ULN.
Creatinine ≤ 1.5 x ULN or CrCl > 30 mL/min; CrCl must be > 50 mL/min for cisplatin (carboplatin if 30-50).

No prior palliative systemic therapy for recurrent/metastatic NPC (prior curative-intent therapy, including systemic therapy before curative re-irradiation or surgery, allowed); > 6 months from last curative-intent treatment to recurrence.
No prior PD-L1, PD-L2, LAG-3, or other checkpoint/co-stimulation agents; prior PD-1 or CTLA-4 inhibitor allowed only as adjuvant or neoadjuvant therapy for non-metastatic NPC.
Prior therapy toxicity resolved to grade 0-1 (except alopecia, dry mouth, dysgeusia, dysphagia, fatigue; cisplatin neuropathy must be grade 0-2; any hearing loss allowed).
No palliative RT within 30 days unless the irradiated sites are not target lesions and not the only measurable disease; no major surgery within 30 days.
No unstable angina requiring hospitalization or MI within 6 months; NYHA II or better; no prior myocarditis.
No history of pneumonitis requiring steroids, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, or organizing pneumonia; no active or MDR TB (treated TB > 2 years ago allowed); no active infection requiring IV therapy.

No active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment within 2 years (vitiligo, type 1 diabetes, hormone-replaced endocrinopathy, alopecia, and psoriasis not requiring systemic therapy allowed); no immunosuppressive steroids (> 10 mg prednisone) or immunosuppressants within 14 days; no prior solid organ or bone marrow transplant.
No live vaccine within 30 days; no grade 3-4 allergy to cisplatin, carboplatin, or gemcitabine, or grade 4 reaction to any monoclonal antibody.

HIV allowed on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months at an experienced site; chronic HBV requires undetectable HBV DNA; HCV must be treated and cured or undetectable on treatment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

Step 3: no progression after a minimum of 3 and up to 6 induction cycles completed within 20 weeks of Cycle 1 Day 1 (fewer than 6 only for toxicity delays or intercurrent illness), CT within 30 days, no criteria for permanent discontinuation or nivolumab-related autoimmune toxicity requiring discontinuation, and post-induction plasma EBV DNA collected.

schema.text: Resectable stage III or IV cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Immunosuppressed (yes vs no, defined in section 3.2). Advanced nodal disease (N3 or in-transit metastases vs other). Disease site (head and neck vs non-head and neck or eyelid).

schema.text: Schema dated 12-SEP-2025.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Standard of care surgery, then adjuvant radiation as indicated.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Neoadjuvant cemiplimab (REGN2810) every 3 weeks for 4 doses, then response-adapted oncologic surgery, then adjuvant radiation as indicated, then adjuvant cemiplimab every 6 weeks for 4 doses. Adjuvant cemiplimab is given after adjuvant radiation when radiation is indicated.

schema.label: Pathologic complete response
schema.text: Patients with a pathologic complete response will not receive adjuvant radiation or adjuvant cemiplimab. Full cemiplimab dosing is in section 5.1 and is not printed on the schema page.

eligibility: Pathologically proven invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, or a regional lymph node or in-transit metastasis of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.

WHO subtypes are eligible when the predominant histology is cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma: spindle cell squamous cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma with sarcomatoid differentiation, acantholytic squamous cell carcinoma, clear cell squamous cell carcinoma, and lymphoepithelial carcinoma. Keratoacanthoma and verrucous subtypes are not eligible.

Regional metastasis without a primary tumor requires a clinical history of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma draining to the involved nodes or in-transit metastases. If that history is ambiguous, tumor genomic sequencing suggesting a cutaneous primary is acceptable (tumor mutation burden at least 10 mutations/Mb, and/or more than 50 percent UV-related mutations, and/or signature 7). Sequencing is not required.

Previously untreated or recurrent disease. Clinical AJCC 8th edition stage III or IV for head and neck sites, or UICC stage III or IV for eyelid and non-head and neck sites. The primary site is head and neck skin, other cutaneous sites, or eyelid skin.
Mucosal squamous cell carcinoma is excluded (vermillion lip, nasal, oral, sinonasal, conjunctival, anogenital).

The tumor must be resectable with curative intent. T4b disease with bony skull base invasion and/or skull base foramen involvement is not eligible. T4b eyelid tumors staged by UICC that do not involve the brain are eligible.
At least one lesion measurable by RECIST 1.1. No definitive clinical or radiologic distant metastatic disease, and no visceral or distant nodal disease.
Age 18 or older. ECOG performance status 0 to 2.

Not pregnant and not nursing. Negative urine or serum pregnancy test within 14 days before registration for persons of childbearing potential. Participants of childbearing potential must use highly effective contraception during therapy and for at least 4 months after study therapy.

Required labs: absolute neutrophil count at least 1,000 cells/mm3, platelets at least 75,000 cells/mm3, and hemoglobin at least 8.0 g/dL (transfusion or other intervention to reach that hemoglobin is allowed).

Creatinine clearance greater than 30 mL/min by Cockcroft-Gault. Total bilirubin at or below 1.5 times the institutional upper limit of normal (at or below 3 times that limit if Gilbert syndrome is documented). AST and ALT at or below 3 times the institutional upper limit of normal.

No prior systemic therapy for the study cancer, including immunotherapy currently given for a separate malignancy. No prior radiotherapy to the region of the study cancer that would make cumulative organ-at-risk doses exceed protocol limits.
No myocardial infarction or unstable angina within 6 months. New York Heart Association class IIb or better is required. Class III or IV is not eligible.
No active infection requiring systemic antibiotics, antivirals, or antifungals. No allogeneic or autologous stem cell transplant. No solid organ transplant other than a corneal transplant.

No active, known, or suspected autoimmune disease, defined as a need for more than 10 mg prednisone daily or equivalent, a need for disease-modifying agents, or significant autoimmune disease treated with systemic immunosuppression within 5 years before registration.

A brief steroid course, type 1 diabetes, endocrinopathies requiring only hormone replacement (including hypothyroidism from autoimmune thyroiditis), and skin disorders such as vitiligo, psoriasis, or alopecia that do not need systemic treatment are allowed. Physiologic replacement at or below 10 mg prednisone daily, and inhaled or topical steroids, are allowed when not given for immunosuppressive intent.
HIV with an undetectable viral load within 6 months on effective antiretroviral therapy is eligible. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia with no anti-CLL therapy within 6 months is eligible.

No history of interstitial lung disease. No active noninfectious pneumonitis requiring immune-suppressive therapy. No active tuberculosis. No live vaccines within 28 days before registration. No history of allergic reaction to the study agent or to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition, including excipients.

On-study guidance: chronic hepatitis B must have an undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated. Hepatitis C must have been treated and cured, or the viral load must be undetectable if treatment is ongoing. A prior or concurrent malignancy is allowed when its natural history or treatment would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

eligibility: Pathologically proven locally recurrent or persistent squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck arising in the oral cavity, oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx.
PD-L1 combined positive score at least 1, from a CLIA-certified laboratory.
Insurance or other payment coverage for neoadjuvant chemotherapy must be verified.
Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1, and the patient must be a candidate for salvage surgery and deemed surgically resectable without gross residual disease.
p16-positive oropharynx: T2, T3, or T4 and N0, N1, or N2. All other eligible patients: T2, T3, or T4a and N0, N1, N2a, N2b, N2c, or N3a, using AJCC 8th edition.

Oral cavity disease is eligible only when it is recurrent or persistent after prior surgery. Candidates for salvage laryngectomy for recurrent laryngeal cancer, done with curative intent, are eligible. Resectable lymph node-only recurrence is eligible.

No major vascular involvement, defined as more than 180 degrees of the common carotid or internal carotid artery, and no jugular foramen or prevertebral or paraspinous muscle involvement that precludes a curative resection. No distant metastatic disease.
Minimum workup: general history and physical examination, plus diagnostic-quality neck CT and PET/CT of the neck (PET with attenuation-correction CT of the neck, chest, and abdomen).
Age 18 or older. ECOG performance status 0 to 2. Not pregnant and not nursing. Negative urine or serum pregnancy test within 30 days before registration for persons of childbearing potential.
Labs: absolute neutrophil count at least 1,500 cells/mm3, platelets at least 100,000 cells/mm3, and hemoglobin at least 8.0 g/dL (transfusion or other intervention is allowed).

Only one prior course of radiation, definitive or postoperative, is allowed. It must have been completed at least 6 months before registration, and the majority of the index persistent or recurrent volume (more than 50 percent) must have received at least 40 Gy.

Prior systemic therapy, including anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 therapy, in the definitive setting (neoadjuvant or adjuvant) is permitted if completed at least 4 months before registration. Prior systemic therapy, including immunotherapy, for recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma is not permitted.

No investigational anticancer agent within 4 weeks before registration. No New York Heart Association class III or IV. No active infection requiring intravenous antibiotics, antivirals, or antifungals. No grade 3 or 4 peripheral neuropathy.
No history of allergic reaction to the study agent, to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition, or to immune checkpoint inhibitors, including excipients.

On-study guidance: HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible. Chronic hepatitis B must have an undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated. Hepatitis C must have been treated and cured, or the viral load must be undetectable if treatment is ongoing. Persistent grade 3 or 4 electrolyte abnormalities must be reversible with replacement. Highly effective contraception is required during therapy and for 4 months after.

schema.label: Population
schema.text: Previously untreated, unresected, locoregionally advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx, hypopharynx, oropharynx, or oral cavity, in patients with a contraindication to cisplatin. The cisplatin contraindication is an eligibility rule in section 3.2.5. The schema box itself names the two concurrent regimens.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: p16 status: p16-positive oropharynx vs p16-negative oropharynx or non-oropharynx. AJCC 9th edition stage: for p16-positive oropharynx, T1-2 and N2 or T3 and N0-2 (stage II) vs T4 or N3 (stage III). For p16-negative oropharynx or non-oropharynx, T1-3 and N0-2b vs T4a-b or N2c-3. ECOG and comorbidities: performance status 0 and modified Charlson comorbidity index 0 vs performance status 1 to 2 or modified Charlson index greater than 0.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Both arms are definitive radiation with concurrent systemic therapy. Section 5, not the schema box, prints the doses below.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Radiation plus concurrent cetuximab. Section 5: cetuximab 400 mg/m2 intravenously within 7 days before day 1 of radiation, then intensity-modulated radiation, 70 Gy in 35 fractions, 5 fractions per week, with cetuximab 250 mg/m2 intravenously weekly during radiation for 7 weekly cycles.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Radiation plus concurrent carboplatin and paclitaxel. Section 5: intensity-modulated radiation, 70 Gy in 35 fractions, 5 fractions per week, with carboplatin AUC 2 plus paclitaxel 40 mg/m2 intravenously weekly for 7 cycles beginning on day 1 of radiation.

schema.label: Radiation technique
schema.text: Section 5.2: intensity-modulated radiation and image guidance are mandatory. Intensity-modulated proton therapy is allowed. Passive scattered proton therapy is not allowed. Protocol treatment must begin within 14 days after registration. The prescription in section 5.2 is 7000 cGy in 35 fractions over 7 weeks.

eligibility: Pathologically confirmed, previously untreated, unresected squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx, hypopharynx, oropharynx, or oral cavity.
Local p16 status is required for all oropharynx patients before registration. Local p16 status is recommended, not required, for non-oropharynx patients.
Non-oropharynx and p16-negative oropharynx must be AJCC 9th edition stage III, IVA, or IVB: T3 N0 or T1-3 N1 M0 (III); T1-3 N2 or T4a N0-N2 M0 (IVA); T4b N0-N2 or T1-4b N3 M0 (IVB).
p16-positive oropharynx must be AJCC 9th edition stage II or III: T3 N0-2 or T1-2 N2 M0 (II); T4 N0-3 or T1-3 N3 M0 (III).

Before registration: head and neck imaging with contrast neck CT or MRI unless contrast is contraindicated, or PET/CT that includes diagnostic-quality contrast CT of the neck unless contrast is contraindicated. Chest imaging with contrast chest CT unless contraindicated, or PET/CT.
Age 18 or older. Before registration, complete the online tool at www.nrgoncology.org and record the modified Charlson comorbidity index, HNCIG omega score, and G-8 score.

A contraindication to cisplatin is required, defined as at least one of the following: creatinine clearance below 60 mL/min by the Cockroft-Gault formula, pre-existing grade 2 or higher sensory or motor neuropathy, or hearing loss (an existing need for a hearing aid, or at least a 25 decibel shift over 2 contiguous frequencies on a pretreatment hearing test as clinically indicated).

Cisplatin ineligibility may instead be age 70 or older with an HNCIG omega score below 0.80. Or age under 70 with all of the following: HNCIG omega score below 0.80, modified Charlson comorbidity index at least 1, and G-8 score 14 or lower.
ECOG performance status 0 to 2. Not pregnant and not nursing.

Participants must be able to safely receive the radiation and drug regimens per the current FDA-approved package inserts, the treating investigator's discretion, and institutional guidelines. Section 3 does not list separate absolute neutrophil count, platelet, hemoglobin, or bilirubin floors.

No prior systemic therapy for the study cancer. Prior systemic therapy for a different cancer is allowed. No prior radiotherapy to the region of the study cancer that would overlap radiation fields. No prior surgery for the study cancer.

On-study guidance: HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible. Chronic hepatitis B must have an undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated. Hepatitis C must have been treated and cured, or the viral load must be undetectable if treatment is ongoing. Persistent grade 3 or 4 electrolyte abnormalities must be reversible with replacement. Highly effective contraception is required during therapy and for 6 months after.

arms.label: Arm 1 (systemic maintenance chemotherapy)
arms.text: Patients may receive docetaxel IV over 60 minutes on day 1, erlotinib hydrochloride by mouth daily, or gemcitabine IV over 30 minutes on days 1 and 8. Patients with non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer may receive pemetrexed disodium IV over 10 minutes on day 1 alone or in combination with pembrolizumab IV over 30 minutes. Courses repeat every 21 days in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

arms.label: Arm 2 (LCT + systemic maintenance chemotherapy)
arms.text: Patients undergo local consolidative therapy (LCT) over 2-5 weeks, consisting of SBRT/hypofractionated radiation to the primary tumor and metastatic sites or surgery of metastatic sites. Hypofractionated radiation using IMRT or 3D-CRT can be given in place of SBRT. Within 2 weeks after completion of LCT (3 weeks if surgery occurred), patients receive chemotherapy as in Arm 1.

schema.label: Population
schema.text: Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer with stable disease or partial response after 4 to 6 cycles of etoposide and platinum plus atezolizumab. For induction, one cycle of etoposide and platinum without atezolizumab is allowed if the patient cannot receive concurrent atezolizumab for every induction cycle.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Number of sites receiving radiation (1 to 3 fields vs more than 3). Partial response vs stable disease. ECOG performance status 0 or 1 vs 2. Brain metastases (no vs yes).

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Schema dated 09-NOV-2022, carried in the March 13, 2025 protocol. Section 5 confirms the radiation doses and the atezolizumab dose.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Atezolizumab maintenance. Section 5: atezolizumab 1200 mg intravenously every 21 days until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Standard radiation, daily, to up to 5 sites, plus atezolizumab maintenance. Thoracic or liver radiation: 45 Gy or 30 Gy. Extra-thoracic radiation: 30 Gy or 20 Gy. Section 5 confirms 45 Gy in 15 fractions (3 Gy, lung or liver only, preferred for lung), 30 Gy in 10 fractions (3 Gy, any site), and 20 Gy in 5 fractions (4 Gy, extra-thoracic metastatic sites only). Radiation starts during the first 5 weeks of maintenance atezolizumab, which is the same 1200 mg every 21 days schedule as Arm 1.

schema.label: Prophylactic cranial irradiation
schema.text: PCI is optional. The schema says co-enrollment on SWOG S1827 (MAVERICK) or NRG-CC003 should be strongly considered. Section 5: PCI may be given during induction chemotherapy before randomization. If PCI is given on study, use 25 Gy in 10 fractions. Atezolizumab does not need to be delayed during PCI. Protocol treatment begins within 21 days after registration.

eligibility: Cytologic, histologic, or pathologic confirmation of extensive-stage small cell lung cancer at a primary or metastatic site.

Partial response or stable disease after 4 to 6 cycles of etoposide and platinum plus atezolizumab, documented on restaging PET/CT, diagnostic CT, or MRI at the treating physician's option. Atezolizumab should continue through randomization.

At least 3 cycles must include etoposide, platinum, and atezolizumab. One induction cycle of etoposide and platinum without concurrent atezolizumab is allowed. Randomize within 9 weeks of the last etoposide and platinum dose if PCI is not given, or within 6 weeks after PCI is completed.
Measurable disease per RECIST, 3 or fewer observable liver metastases, and no progressive disease per RECIST at enrollment.
A pleural effusion is allowed if thoracentesis is cytologically negative, or if the fluid volume is too small to sample and the effusion does not show increased metabolic activity on CT/PET.

History and physical examination within 14 days before registration. Imaging within 42 days before registration: MRI or CT of the brain with contrast, and CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis or whole-body PET/CT any time after the fourth cycle of chemotherapy and before registration.
Age 18 or older. ECOG performance status 0 to 2 within 14 days before registration.

Labs within 14 days: absolute neutrophil count at least 1,000 cells/mm3, platelets at least 75,000 cells/mm3, hemoglobin at least 8 g/dL, and total bilirubin at or below 1.5 times the upper limit of normal.

AST and ALT at or below 3 times the upper limit of normal, or at or below 5 times that limit if the liver is involved. Alkaline phosphatase at or below 2.5 times the upper limit of normal, or at or below 5 times that limit with documented liver involvement or bone metastases. Creatinine clearance at least 40 mL/min by Cockcroft-Gault.
Upfront radiation to a symptomatic metastatic site is allowed for pain or impending fracture.

Brain metastases are eligible after whole-brain radiation given before enrollment, at any time during induction systemic therapy, with hippocampal sparing or 3D conformal technique. After that radiotherapy the patient must be neurologically stable (for example, not having uncontrolled seizures) and must not need steroids above 10 mg of prednisone daily.

Negative serum or urine pregnancy test within 14 days before registration for women of childbearing potential. Women of childbearing potential and men must use adequate contraception before entry, during study treatment, and for 5 months (150 days) after the last dose of study agent. Women who are breastfeeding and unwilling to discontinue are not eligible.

HIV-positive patients are eligible on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months and a stable HAART regimen, and with no concurrent antibiotics or antifungal agents for prevention of opportunistic infections.
Study-specific informed consent, or consent by a legally authorized representative, is required before study entry.
Not eligible: more than 3 liver metastases, disease invading the heart, or more than 10 metastatic sites detectable after induction systemic therapy. Each visible bone metastasis counts as one site.

No concurrent malignancy whose natural history or treatment could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment of atezolizumab or radiation. No prior thoracic radiotherapy that would overlap fields, unless the overlap meets acceptable normal-tissue dose constraints.

No active autoimmune disease, including systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, antiphospholipid thrombosis, Wegener granulomatosis, Sjogren syndrome, Guillain-Barre syndrome, multiple sclerosis, vasculitis, or glomerulonephritis. Inactive autoimmune disease for more than 3 years, without methotrexate or steroids above 10 mg prednisone daily equivalent, is eligible. Autoimmune hypothyroidism on stable thyroid replacement, and controlled type 1 diabetes on stable insulin, are eligible. Eczema, psoriasis, lichen simplex chronicus, or vitiligo is excluded only when there is active disease with acute exacerbation and immunosuppressive medication within 12 months before enrollment.

No active tuberculosis. No known clinically significant liver disease, including active viral, alcoholic, or other hepatitis, cirrhosis, fatty liver, or inherited liver disease. Resolved hepatitis B (negative HBsAg and positive anti-HBc) is eligible. Hepatitis C antibody is eligible only if HCV RNA PCR is negative.

No known immunosuppressive disease, for example prior bone marrow transplant or chronic lymphocytic leukemia. No COPD requiring chronic oral steroid therapy above 10 mg prednisone daily or equivalent at registration. Inhaled corticosteroids are not exclusionary.

No unstable angina or congestive heart failure requiring hospitalization within 3 months. No myocardial infarction within 6 months. No clinically significant interstitial lung disease. No history of allogeneic organ transplant. No immunotherapy-induced pneumonitis.

schema.text: Locally advanced inoperable node-positive non-small cell lung cancer, stage II or III.
