schema.text: PD-L1 expression (under 1%, 1% to 49%, 50% to 100%) and T stage (T1-T2a versus T2b or higher).

schema.label: Arm 1
schema.text: Radiotherapy to all known thoracic disease, 60 Gy in 2 Gy fractions, with concurrent chemotherapy, then consolidation immunotherapy for up to 12 months.

schema.label: Arm 2
schema.text: SBRT to the primary tumor, then radiotherapy to nodal metastases, 60 Gy in 2 Gy fractions, with concurrent chemotherapy, then consolidation immunotherapy for up to 12 months. The protocol lists the allowed SBRT fractionation.

eligibility: Pathologically proven stage IIB or III node-positive non-small cell lung cancer, AJCC 8th edition, with known PD-L1 status before registration. A primary tumor and at least one nodal metastasis are required.
Up to 4 cycles of systemic therapy for this cancer before registration are allowed. Prior chemotherapy for a different cancer is allowed.
Patients who refuse surgery, and patients who are unresectable or medically inoperable, are eligible. Separate nodules in the same lobe as the primary are eligible.
No distant metastases on FDG PET/CT. Primary tumor 7 cm or smaller. Age 18 or older. ECOG 0-2.
Blood counts must be adequate for chemotherapy and radiotherapy, at the treating physician's discretion. Creatinine clearance at least 25 mL/min by Cockcroft-Gault.
A non-malignant pleural effusion is allowed if it is not a known exudate. A visible effusion needs a negative cytology. A minimal effusion that cannot be tapped safely is allowed.

A prior or concurrent malignancy is allowed when it is not expected to interfere with safety or efficacy assessment. A negative pregnancy test within 14 days is required when relevant, and consent is required.
No prior radiotherapy to this cancer, and no prior radiotherapy to the region that would overlap fields and impede treatment.
Patients without an identifiable primary and at least one node are not eligible. T3-4 N0 and T0 N1-3 are not eligible.

A central primary under 2 cm from involved nodal disease that would make the SBRT and nodal fields overlap the proximal bronchial tree or esophagus is not eligible, with the exception stated for segmental nodes.
Pregnant participants, and participants unwilling to stop breastfeeding or to use highly effective contraception for the labeled interval after the chosen systemic therapy, are not eligible.

registry_schema.text: Early assessment of the efficacy of anti-cancer therapy is highly desirable and an unmet need in clinical oncology. Currently, treatment efficacy is mostly measured by following tumor size by anatomical imaging (CT scan or MRI). However, changes in tumor size may be observed only after several weeks to several months after completion of treatment. Meanwhile, in cases where there is no response, the patient is unnecessarily exposed to treatment's side effects, and precious time may be lost before the initiation of an alternative, potentially more beneficial line of therapy. registry_schema.text: This is a Phase 2 trial testing the safety and effectiveness of NTS-WBRT (normal tissue sparing whole brain radiation therapy) in treating brain metastases. NTS-WBRT is a targeted radiation therapy that further reduces radiation dose to tissue that does not need radiation therapy treatment. The research study procedures include screening for eligibility and study treatment including evaluations and follow up visits. It is expected that about 41 people will take part in this research study.

registry_schema.text: The brain is frequently a site of disease relapse in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) patients. registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: Radiation therapy (RT) is an effective treatment for patients with advanced-stage clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). Current evidence has shown promising outcomes combining radiation therapy and standard systemic therapy in patients with metastatic/recurrent ccRCC. CAIX is a highly sensitive and specific biomarker expressed on ccRCC and in previous studies the investigators have shown excellent diagnostic efficacy of 68Ga-NY104, a CAIX-targeted PET tracer, in patients with metastatic ccRCC. In this study, the investigators aim to investigate the effect of 68Ga-NY104, and 18F-FDG PET/CT guided RT combining standard systemic therapy in patients with metastatic ccRCC.

schema.text: Single-arm phase II trial for veterans with de novo oligometastatic prostate cancer. Primary endpoint is the percent of patients with PSA under 0.05 ng/mL six months after testosterone recovers to at least 150 ng/dL. Evaluable sample size is 25, total 28 allowing for testosterone non-recovery. Protocol version 3, 26 March 2018.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Radical prostatectomy with pelvic node dissection first. If pT3a or higher, positive margins, or N1, postoperative IMRT to pelvic nodes 45 to 50.4 Gy and prostate bed 66 to 72 Gy in conventional fractionation. Within 0 to 3 days after surgery: one 45 mg subcutaneous leuprolide depot, apalutamide 240 mg orally daily, and abiraterone 1000 mg orally daily with prednisone 10 mg daily, for six months. SBRT to all visible M1a/b sites within two months of starting androgen deprivation. Recommended SBRT is 6 to 8 Gy x 5, 9 to 12 Gy x 3, or 16 to 18 Gy x 1. A BED above 100 Gy (alpha/beta 3) is a goal but not required.

brief.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Parikh et al., BMC Cancer 2019 (PMID 30935383). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Biopsy-proven prostate adenocarcinoma, age at least 18, M1a/b with 1 to 5 visible metastases on NaF PET/CT or PSMA PET/CT plus CT chest/abdomen/pelvis. Pelvic nodes of any number are allowed if the largest is under 2 cm. No visceral metastases. ECOG 0 or 1. Testosterone above 200 ng/dL before androgen deprivation. Fit for prostatectomy, metastasis SBRT, and androgen deprivation.

Hemoglobin at least 9.0 g/dL and platelets at least 100,000 x 10^9/microliter as printed, both independent of transfusion or growth factors within 3 months. Albumin at least 3.0 g/dL, GFR at least 45 mL/min, potassium at least 3.5 mmol/L, bilirubin at most 1.5 times the upper limit, AST or ALT under 2.5 times the upper limit. The printed platelet unit is not restated as a corrected value.

Biopsy of one metastasis should be attempted unless unsafe. If not diagnostic, a second imaging modality must agree. Excluded: small-cell histology, spinal cord compression, prior pelvic malignancy or pelvic radiation, inflammatory bowel disease, seizure history, and specified cardiovascular events within 6 months.

pretreatment.item: NaF or PSMA PET/CT with CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis
pretreatment.note: PSA and total testosterone are also drawn at inclusion.

during.item: PSA, testosterone, quality of life, and toxicity
during.note: Pill counts monthly during the six months of apalutamide and abiraterone. SBRT is given between day 30 and day 60. Systemic therapy stops at 6 months. CTCAE version 4.

followup.window: Every 30 days for the first year, then every 3 months
followup.note: Patients remain on study until unacceptable toxicity, progression, withdrawal, or two years. PSA and testosterone continue every 3 months after the first year on the visit table.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Randomized phase II trial (ORATOR). Primary endpoint is MDADI quality of life at 1 year. Sample size is 68. Toxicity uses NCI-CTC version 4.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: 1:1 to radiotherapy with or without chemotherapy, or transoral robotic surgery with or without adjuvant therapy.

arms.label: Radiotherapy
arms.text: IMRT. Gross disease 70 Gy in 35 fractions over 7 weeks, optional high-risk nodes 63 Gy in 35 fractions, low-risk nodes 56 Gy in 35 fractions. N0 disease receives radiotherapy alone. N1 to 2 disease receives concurrent cisplatin 100 mg/m2 every 3 weeks. If unfit, the cisplatin dose or schedule may change, or cetuximab or weekly carboplatin AUC 1.5 may be used. Accelerated or hyperfractionated delivery of the same doses in 6 weeks is allowed.

arms.label: Transoral robotic surgery
arms.text: TORS and selective neck dissection, which may be staged within 3 weeks. Positive margins or extranodal extension: 64 Gy in 30 fractions to that region, 60 Gy in 30 fractions to the operative bed and positive neck, and 54 Gy in 30 fractions to low-risk nodes, with cisplatin 100 mg/m2 every 3 weeks or weekly carboplatin AUC 1.5 if unfit. Adjuvant radiotherapy without chemotherapy is recommended for any positive node, lymphovascular invasion, pT3 or pT4, or margins under 2 mm. Perineural invasion alone does not require radiotherapy.

Excluded: serious comorbidity, prior head and neck cancer within 5 years, any prior head and neck radiation, metastatic disease, another invasive cancer unless disease-free for 5 years (non-melanoma skin cancer allowed), inability to complete questionnaires, and pregnancy or lactation.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Open-label multicenter randomized phase II trial (ORATOR2). Primary endpoint is overall survival of each arm versus historical control, with a hypothesized 2-year overall survival of at least 85%. Sample size is 140. Version 1.3, 15 March 2019.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Smoking history, under 10 versus at least 10 pack-years.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: 1:1 permuted blocks. Treatment starts within 4 weeks of randomization.

arms.label: De-escalated radiotherapy
arms.text: 60 Gy in 30 fractions to gross tumor and involved nodes, 54 Gy in 30 fractions to high-risk subclinical areas, and 48 Gy in 30 fractions to low-risk nodes. Node-negative disease or a single node under 3 cm: accelerated radiotherapy over 5 weeks with six fractions a week. Multiple nodes or one node over 3 cm: daily radiotherapy over 6 weeks with weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 for six cycles. Patients older than 70 may receive standard fractionation. If unfit for cisplatin, cetuximab or weekly carboplatin AUC 1.5 may be used.

arms.label: Transoral surgery
arms.text: Transoral resection and selective neck dissection. If extranodal extension or positive margins: 60 Gy, 54 Gy, and 48 Gy in 30 fractions over 6 weeks to the high-risk site, operative bed, and undissected low-risk neck. Without those factors but with other risk factors: 50 Gy and 45 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks. Adjuvant chemoradiation is not given unless gross disease remains and the patient would have received chemotherapy on the radiotherapy arm. Perineural invasion alone: adjuvant radiotherapy is discretionary.

brief.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Nichols et al., BMC Cancer 2020 (PMID 32059705). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age at least 18, ECOG 0 to 2, HPV-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (p16, PCR, or in situ hybridization). AJCC 8th edition T1 or T2 and N0, N1, or N2, likely negative margins.

If chemotherapy may be required, within 4 weeks: neutrophils above 1.5 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin above 80 g/L, platelets above 100 x 10^9/L, bilirubin under 35 micromol/L, AST and ALT under 3 times the upper limit, creatinine under 130 micromol/L or clearance at least 50 mL/min.

Excluded: unambiguous extranodal extension or matted nodes, prior head and neck radiotherapy or cancer within 5 years, metastatic disease, another invasive cancer within 5 years except non-melanoma skin cancer, and pregnancy or lactation.
